title: Partly pooled monthly error scales improved sea-level log scores at 159 gauges in 2010-2024
abstract: We tested fixed calendar-month error scales for annual-issued forecasts of monthly mean relative sea level. We used 159 long-record PSMSL gauges and 28,470 target months in 2010-2024. Calibration errors from 1990-2009 set each variance to half the calendar-month mean square plus half the all-month mean square. The mean Gaussian log score gain over one constant scale was 0.0362 nats per month. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 0.0288 to 0.0439. Equal weight for 43 geographic cells gave a gain of 0.0216. The 10 southern gauges gave no clear gain. Nominal 90% coverage rose from 91.14% to 91.82%, so better scores did not improve all calibration measures. The result supports seasonal error scales in this selected sample. Revised records, uneven geography, Gaussian assumptions and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Source records remain external. Code, exact source hashes, original aggregate evidence and a figure are included.

display.caption: Partly pooled monthly error scales gave positive mean log score gains at 159 gauges and under cell weights. The 10 southern gauges gave no clear gain. Site means varied, and overall range coverage did not move closer to its 90% target.

citations.reason: Prior four-site seasonal error-scale test set the question. Source data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
Prior annual-issued mean forecast design and sample-quality rules informed this test. No code or fitted output was reused.
